title: Writing-to-read lesson sequence with speed-practice and simulated e-mail activities
description: The program's instructional pattern moves from sound-level to text-level production: lessons "begin by having students say and write individual sounds and the letters that represent those sounds, and then progress to having students write words, sentences, and stories." Two supplementary activities extend the pattern: the Power Fountain activity for practicing "speed and accuracy in writing and typing" after attaining a certain level, and the E-mail Tower, "a simulated e-mail program," for practicing newly acquired skills by writing short messages. Teachers or parents can print individual or group progress reports.
requirements: The software plus corresponding activity book lessons; a teacher or parent able to print progress reports; computer access at school or home
constraints: Speed and accuracy practice via the Power Fountain activity is available only after students attain a certain level; the E-mail Tower is described as optional
target_learners: Beginning readers aged six to nine
target_learning_goals: Sounding out, typing, and writing words, sentences, and stories
examples: The evaluated implementation paired teacher-led warm-up activities from the teacher's manual with individual computer practice of the same skills
key_sources: What Works Clearinghouse, U.S. Department of Education. (2007). WWC Intervention Report: Read, Write & Type!™. http://www.fcrr.org/TechnicalReports/RWTfullrept.pdf
grain_size: lesson-to-unit sequence within a software curriculum
